examples.question: What does E-365 mean?
examples.answer: Meaning: The hydraulic oil is running too hot. In our system the warning starts above 90 °C and becomes critical above 95 °C (our assumed limits). Normal working range is about 55–78 °C. Likely causes: long periods of heavy digging or holding the relief valve (pushing against a stop), a blocked hydraulic oil cooler, low hydraulic oil level, a hot day, or internal wear in the pump or valves. A slow rise over days together with unsteady pressure is an early sign of a hydraulic failure.

examples.question: What does E-360 mean?
examples.answer: Meaning: The hydraulic tank level is low. In our data this code often appears together with a sudden hydraulic pressure drop, which usually means a leak (a burst hose, loose fitting or damaged cylinder seal). Likely causes: a leaking or burst hydraulic hose, a loose fitting, a damaged cylinder seal, or oil not topped up after service.

examples.question: Why doesn't the system just shut the machine off when it overheats?
examples.answer: Safe action first: you stay in control: lower the load and get to level ground before any shutdown. A sudden automatic stop can be more dangerous than the fault itself. The machine may be holding a load in the air, travelling, or working on a slope. Stopping the engine can remove power steering, hydraulic control or brake assist at the wrong moment. So the system warns, suggests reduced power, then guides a safe shutdown, and escalates to the site manager if nothing changes.

examples.question: Someone walked behind my excavator. What do I do?
examples.answer: Stop all movement (travel, swing and attachment). Sound the horn. Do not move again until you can see the person and they have moved to a safe place, or a    spotter signals it is clear. If people keep walking near the machine, tell your supervisor so a pedestrian zone or barrier    can be set up, and note it in your handover.

examples.question: I feel very sleepy on night shift. What should I do?
examples.answer: Finish the current movement safely, then stop: lower the attachment and park on level ground. Take a break of at least 15 minutes out of the cab: walk, drink water, eat something light. Tell your supervisor. The app will already have suggested a break and notified them when the    level is high, and the task plan will be adjusted to fit the break. Do not rely on an open window, loud music or strong tea to keep going. They don't remove fatigue. In our site data, most near misses happen late in night shifts, when fatigue is highest.

examples.question: How can I use less fuel on my wheel loader?
examples.answer: Cut idle time. High idle (above about 1200 rpm) burns 6–8 litres per hour doing nothing; low   idle burns 2–4. If you wait more than about 10 minutes, shut down (once parked safely and, for a   hot engine, after a 3–5 minute cool-down). Use the right power mode. Economy mode is enough for most loading, grading and backfilling.   Use full power only for hard digging or steep climbs. Plan short cycles. Place trucks and piles to keep swing angles and travel distances short. Avoid holding the relief valve.
